data.title: Perún's Grove near Úbrež – a Slavic cult place
data.excerpt: Many readers know Eduard Hvižďák's account of Perúnov háj pri Úbreži, a grove first mentioned in a charter of 1327. This is a short summary of what his long-running amateur research has established about the supposed sanctuary of Perún – a place that archaeology has so far failed to confirm.
data.metaTitle: Perún's Grove near Úbrež – a Slavic cult place
data.metaDescription: A summary of the puzzling site of Perún's Grove near Úbrež in eastern Slovakia and of the amateur research carried out there by Eduard Hvižďák.

keyFacts.label: Site
keyFacts.value: Úbrež, the Vihorlat Mountains – an oak grove by the hamlet of „U Brehu Perúnového hája“

keyFacts.label: Theme
keyFacts.value: A sanctuary dedicated to Perún, oriented according to the four elements

timeline.title: First written mention
timeline.description: Perún's Grove near Úbrež is mentioned for the first time in a charter on the demarcation of the boundaries between the estates of two noblemen.

timeline.title: Archaeological survey
timeline.description: In the spring of 2011 archaeologists surveyed the surface of the sanctuary with a metal detector and found no metal object, which matches the rule that the sacred precinct was to be entered without metal.

timeline.title: Demise of the sanctuary
timeline.description: The digging of a drainage channel below Kárna dried out Perún's Grove, and with it the boundaries of the sacred precinct and its energy field ceased to exist.

children.text: Many of you will certainly know the splendid account by Mr Eduard Hvižďák,
Perúnov háj pri Úbreži (Perún's Grove near Úbrež).

Mr Hvižďák, who has been devoting himself to this remarkable site and to its amateur investigation for quite some time, sent me a great deal of material relating to the grove. It would be a pity not to share it with other readers as well. I therefore offer a short summary of what Mr Hvižďák has established so far. The charter in which Perún's Grove near Úbrež is mentioned for the first time dates from 1327 and concerns the demarcation of the boundaries between the estates of two noblemen. The tradition of Perún's Grove here was evidently very strong, since it survived as late as the 14th century.

blocks.text:
A few years ago I found out by chance that there is a written mention connected with Úbrež in which Perún's Grove is mentioned. Since I have a little more free time in winter, I began to take an interest in it, mainly in the information, and I started walking the ground, as I live here. At first I too thought, like everyone else, that some cult objects might be found there. I thought there would be swords, lances, spears, since it is a sanctuary with the cult of Perún. Last year two archaeologists surveyed it with metal detectors and there was not a gram of iron at the site of the sanctuary, and by the burial mounds we found one rusty size-60 nail, probably from when they were laying out a vineyard there.
Then I got in touch with www.vedy.sk, and the gentleman who runs that site arranged a meeting for me with the supreme Slavic pagan priest Alexander Pater Dij from Omsk, who, as it happened, visited this sanctuary during his tour of Europe and who, after I had shown him my material, confirmed to me 100 % that this sanctuary is genuine, and who found stones with runic signs not far from the sanctuary. He essentially knew what to look for, what it really looked like and how it actually worked, because among them it still functions to this day. He explained to me how our ancestors thought, not how we think. Our understanding and our questions are miles away from what it actually served for and how it served.
Many people ask me how things proceeded in that Perún's Grove in ancient times. People came to the hamlet of „U Brehu Perúnového hája“ from the western side, I think from the large Slavic settlement of Hnojné. For people from more distant parts, the direction towards the central sanctuary was shown by Mount Vihorlat, the highest, dominant hill of the Vihorlat range. In the hamlet of „U Brehu Perúnového hája“ people were given instructions about the programme. Above the hamlet of „U Brehu Perúnového hája“, on the Rika, there were two reservoirs, Veľký and Malý Vir. Entry was from the west towards the east. The ford no longer exists, today there is a concrete bridge there, and neither do Veľký and Malý Vír, because the river Rika was drained and dried out. To this day the Rika is held to be sacred in the awareness of the local people. The sanctuary was entered barefoot, in clothing made only of natural materials /hemp, flax/, without silver, gold, iron, weapons etc., and with the hair loose. The path through the oak grove was lined on both the left and the right side with stones covered in runic signs, and further stones were worked so that they fitted into one another like a jigsaw. In the middle of the oak grove was the sanctuary, where sacred fires of oak wood burned in Perún's circle, and the idol was placed where strong positive energy wells up out of the ground. Visitors to this sanctuary stood facing north /Mount Vihorlat/ and with their backs to the south, in accordance with the teaching of the Slavs. The positive energy field is bounded on the south-western side by the hamlet of „U Brehu“ and on the north-eastern side by the barrow cemetery, plus watercourses around the whole perimeter. The strongest point of this positive zone lies in the middle of the sanctuary beneath the idol. Here rites were held at which people swore and made vows in honour of Perún. The participant entered from the west, across the water. From the west, because our ancestors understood the place where the sun sets as the underworld, and across the water, because water was the boundary of Perún's Grove. To this day the saying has survived that someone is “across the water”. They walked along a path oriented from west to east, because they understood the east as the place where the sun rises, as the heavens. That is why the sanctuary was oriented towards the eastern side and was entered from the western side. Older buildings, i.e. churches, are still oriented in this way today. People entered barefoot so that they could take in positive energy, because shoes act as an insulator. Hair also takes in positive energy, while metal objects disturb and degrade positive energy. That is why people entered without them.
In the spring of 2011 the surface of the sanctuary was surveyed by archaeologists with a metal detector and no object of metal origin was found, so it is no coincidence that nothing of the kind was found there, because nothing like that was even permitted to be there. The sanctuary was placed in an oak grove, because the oak as a tree is dedicated to Perún; where the greatest concentration of positive energy was, they established that place as the centre of a circular structure. The circle was marked only with small stones, or with a groove in the ground. With a groove in the ground they marked the boundary of the energy place. Circular structures were used to replenish bodily energy and for ritual purposes. In the sanctuary fires of oak wood burned in a circle. According to the teaching of our ancestors, i.e. there are four elements: fire, water, air and earth. Fire - Perún - South, water - Lada - West, air - Stribog - East and earth - Veles - North. This sanctuary, i.e. Perún's Grove, was built according to this teaching, which means an oak grove, fires of oak wood and an idol made of oak wood that had been struck by lightning, i.e. under the sign of Perún, i.e. Perún, on the earth, i.e. Veles, surrounded by air, i.e. Stribog, and bounded around the whole perimeter by water, i.e. Lada. Water protects and purifies Perún's Grove. In the sanctuary fires burned in honour of Perún on the earth - Veles - and bounded around the whole perimeter by water, i.e. Lada, and air, Stribog. The fifth element is fate, i.e. Mokoš. That is why the hamlet of „ U Brehu“ is on the western side across the water, and the purification was also carried out from the western side of the reservoir. The burial mounds are on the north-eastern side across the water on a gentle rise, because the sun rises there - the Heavens. On the northern side of Perún's Grove, circular features - burial mounds - can be seen on aerial photographs, north Veles, the guardian of the underworld.. I believe that high-ranking spiritual persons are buried there, by cremation, right beside the barrow cemetery across the water. No activity other than ritual was permitted in Perún's Grove.
The destruction of the sanctuary.
Because a drainage channel was dug below Kárna, the whole of Perún's Grove was drained and dried out, and with that the boundaries of the sacred grove were removed and the positive energy field was destroyed. There was no reservoir for purifying the body before entry and there was no drinking water either, and the sanctuary lacked the fourth element - water - Lada, and with this the sanctuary no longer met the conditions of the teaching of the Slavs - the four elements. The First Military Survey mentions that on the bare hill of Debra the soldiers record a „rušička“ /a wooden church/ of the Eastern rite. Did it disturb the positive energy?
blocks.author: Eduard Hvižďák

children.text: In closing I would only add that the sanctuary has not yet been confirmed archaeologically. Should anything change in this respect in the future, we will certainly be among the first to let you know.
